# Test fixtures

`minimal.epub`, `css-edge-cases.epub`, and `drm-fonts.epub` are small
synthetic fixtures used for fast, targeted unit tests (see `pdf_tests.rs`,
`epub_tests.rs`). `css-edge-cases.epub` has a wide unwrapped `<pre><code>`
block and a CSS `column-count` layout, purpose-built to exercise Chrome
print's lack of "shrink to fit" (see `wide_pre_blocks_wrap_instead_of_clipping`).
`drm-fonts.epub` has two fonts obfuscated with the standard IDPF and Adobe
EPUB font-obfuscation schemes, generated independently of this codebase's
own deobfuscation code (see `deobfuscates_both_font_obfuscation_schemes`).

`doctype-nav.epub` and `doctype-ncx.epub` carry a DOCTYPE in their EPUB3
nav and EPUB2 NCX TOC documents respectively. Real EPUBs very commonly do
(the NISO ncx DOCTYPE, `<!DOCTYPE html>`), but every Gutenberg fixture here
happens not to, which is why a DTD-rejection bug silently wiped the table
of contents for a long time without any test noticing.

`text-entities.epub` has a deliberately non-well-formed chapter (an
unclosed `<br>`, undeclared HTML named entities like `&nbsp;`/`&mdash;`) to
force `htmltext.rs`'s regex fallback path rather than its normal roxmltree
fast path - the only fixture that exercises it (see
`txt_tests.rs::decodes_entities_and_drops_script_and_style`).

`nested-nav.epub` is a minimal fixture whose EPUB3 nav document lives at
`OEBPS/text/nav.xhtml` (not the content-directory root, unlike every other
fixture here) with chapter TOC hrefs written relative to `text/` - the only
fixture that pins down `TocNode.href` being relative to the nav document's
own directory, not `content_dir` (see `epub_output_tests.rs`'s
`nested_toc_directory_keeps_hrefs_valid`).

`minimal.azw3` is `minimal.epub` converted by the bundled `boko` binary,
used by `kindle_tests.rs` to assert Kindle-format input parses to the same
`DocumentIR` as its EPUB source. Regenerate with
`boko convert minimal.epub minimal.azw3` after running
`rust/scripts/fetch-boko.sh`.

## PDF-input fixtures (`pdf_input_tests.rs`)

Every one of these except `real-book.pdf` was generated by running this
project's own `PdfOutput` (bundled headless Chromium) over a small
hand-written EPUB — a deliberate choice (see the PDF-input plan): it gives
exact control over fonts/sizes/columns/headers and produces a real
text-layer PDF with a real outline, at zero new tooling cost. The source
EPUB for each is committed alongside its PDF so regeneration is exact, not
approximate.

- `minimal-text.pdf` — `minimal.epub` (already committed above) converted
  directly: `anyform convert minimal.epub minimal-text.pdf`. Carries
  `minimal.epub`'s own real EPUB3 nav as a PDF outline, so this is what
  pins the outline-preferred chapter-splitting path (over the font-size
  heuristic) in `minimal_text_pdf_splits_by_its_own_outline_with_real_text`.
- `heading-tiers.epub`/`.pdf` — one chapter with three known font sizes
  (24pt/14pt/9.5pt-ish as actually rendered — Chrome's own line-height math
  shifts the nominal 24/16/11pt CSS slightly) plus a paragraph whose final
  line happens to average out just above the *original* 1.15× heading-ratio
  threshold. Regenerate: `anyform convert heading-tiers.epub
  heading-tiers.pdf`. This fixture caught a real false-positive — a
  paragraph's last line ("document.") was getting promoted to its own
  heading — which is why `HEADING_SIZE_RATIO` in `pdf_layout.rs` is 1.3,
  not 1.15; `heading_tiers_pdf_detects_headings_at_known_sizes_without_false_positives`
  pins both the real headings and the absence of that false one.
- `two-column.epub`/`.pdf` — CSS `column-count: 2` over enough filler text
  to actually wrap into two visible columns. Regenerate: `anyform convert
  two-column.epub two-column.pdf`. Pins the multi-column rejection path
  (`two_column_pdf_is_rejected_with_a_specific_message`) — and was the
  fixture that caught a real bug: `detect_columns` originally measured
  coverage from `group_lines`' *merged* same-row lines (which necessarily
  span the whole row, gutter included, since a two-column row's left and
  right text get merged into one `Line` by design — see
  `two_column_page_yields_two_lines_per_row_not_interleaved`), so it never
  saw a real gap and let scrambled interleaved text through unrejected.
  Fixed by building the coverage histogram from raw glyph positions
  instead of merged-line spans.
- `no-text-layer.epub`/`.pdf` — a single full-bleed `<img>` and no text at
  all (uses `minimal.epub`'s own tiny placeholder cover image). Regenerate:
  `anyform convert no-text-layer.epub no-text-layer.pdf`. Pins the
  scanned/image-only rejection path
  (`scanned_pdf_is_rejected_with_a_specific_message`). Note
  `SCANNED_IMAGE_RATIO_THRESHOLD` in `pdf_input.rs` is 0.3, not the more
  intuitive 0.5 — measured live, a full-bleed image inside `PdfOutput`'s
  own default page margins only covers ~45% of the physical page, so a 50%
  threshold would have missed this exact fixture (and, by the same logic,
  a real scan with generous margins).
- `running-heads.epub`/`.pdf` — one long chapter (enough filler text to
  print ~26 pages) converted with `include_headers: true`, a `PDFOptions`
  flag `anyform-cli` doesn't expose on the command line. Regenerate with a
  short throwaway program instead:
  ```rust
  let mut opts = anyform_core::Options::new();
  opts.set("include_headers", anyform_core::Value::Bool(true), anyform_core::Priority::UserSet);
  anyform_doc::document_registry()
      .convert(Path::new("running-heads.epub"), Path::new("running-heads.pdf"), &opts, &anyform_core::StdLog)
      .unwrap();
  ```
  Pins `strip_running_heads` actually firing at real scale — unstripped,
  the repeated header would appear 26+ times;
  `running_heads_pdf_strips_the_repeated_header_across_most_pages` asserts
  it collapses to a handful. **Known, disclosed limitation, not fully
  fixed**: on a page where the header sits unusually close to the first
  body line, `group_lines` can merge them into one `Line` before
  `strip_running_heads` ever sees a clean, separable header line to match
  against — a fragment of the header text can survive, mid-sentence, with
  mangled spacing. The test asserts a dramatic reduction, not perfection.
- `encrypted.pdf` — `minimal-text.pdf` encrypted with a real user password
  via [`qpdf`](https://qpdf.sourceforge.io/) (`brew install qpdf`).
  Regenerate: `qpdf --encrypt testpass ownerpass123 256 --
  minimal-text.pdf encrypted.pdf` (a non-empty owner password is required
  or qpdf refuses as insecure). Pins
  `encrypted_pdf_is_rejected_with_a_specific_message` — the password
  itself (`testpass`) is never used anywhere, only that pdfium's load
  fails with a password error when none is supplied.
- `real-book.pdf` — the one fixture in this set genuinely never produced
  by this engine, so the suite isn't only testing its own output's
  idiosyncrasies. *The Constitution of the United States of America:
  Analysis and Interpretation* (a U.S. government work, public domain
  under 17 U.S.C. § 105), fetched from
  [govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GPO-CONAN-2017/pdf/GPO-CONAN-2017-2.pdf).
  Real single-column legal/government typesetting surfaced two more real
  bugs: a double-space artifact where the word-gap heuristic and a PDF's
  own real space glyph both fired for the same gap (fixed in
  `build_line`), and — not fixed, disclosed instead — an occasional
  stylized enlarged-first-letter run (e.g. "of America" extracting as "ofA
  merica") that `real_third_party_government_pdf_converts_with_readable_text`
  deliberately doesn't assert against, since it's narrow and cosmetic
  against an otherwise legible document, not a comprehension-breaking bug.

The rest are real books used by `real_book_tests.rs`, a regression suite
against actual, structurally diverse content instead of only the synthetic
fixture. All are public domain, downloaded from
[Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/), and safe to redistribute
in git history:

- `doctor-dolittle.epub` - *The Story of Doctor Dolittle* by Hugh Lofting
  ([gutenberg.org/ebooks/501](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/501)).
  Image-heavy: illustrated by the author throughout.
- `pride-and-prejudice.epub` - *Pride and Prejudice* by Jane Austen
  ([gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/1342)).
  A long, many-chapter plain-text novel.
- `origin-of-species.epub` - *On the Origin of Species* by Charles Darwin
  ([gutenberg.org/ebooks/2009](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/2009)).
  Has real footnotes, a glossary, and a large back-of-book index.
- `scientific-american-supplement.epub` - *Scientific American Supplement*,
  Feb 24 1877 ([gutenberg.org/ebooks/19406](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/19406)).
  Has real `<table>` markup: price lists and a paginated table of contents.
